reason: E2 shows a stress-dependent transition from diffusion to dislocation creep in HEAs, supporting the general mechanism switch, but none of the cited evidence directly links interfacial SRO or lattice distortion to this transition or to the predicted two-stage creep response in multilayers. E1 and E3 discuss lattice distortion and SRO in bulk HEAs, not at multilayer interfaces, and do not address creep behavior.
premises: SRO and lattice distortion at interfaces govern the creep mechanism transition
High SRO/distortion inhibits dislocation glide, favoring diffusion creep at low stress
Less distorted regions switch to dislocation glide/climb as stress/temperature increase
Creep exhibits a two-stage response: diffusion-dominated then dislocation-mediated
Higher interfacial SRO/distortion delays dislocation activity and lowers creep rate
